newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance closes in on forest petition numbers.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance closes in on forest petition numbers.

text.p: The opposition Alliance said on Tuesday it would get 240,000 signatures by Wednesday in its bid to force a non-binding referendum on the sale of Forestry Corporation.
But the party plans to continue the petition to give itself a comfort zone to cover any invalid signatures.
It said on Monday it had collected 220,000 signatures.
To force a referendum it would need valid signatures from at least ten percent of all registered voters -- estimated to number 2.4 million.
The National-led government sold the corporation for a net $1.6 billion in August to a consortium led by Fletcher Forests.
The left wing Alliance and economic nationalist New Zealand First have pledged to buy the corporation back if they are in government after the October 12 election.
But they will need the support of Labour which opposed the timing of the sale but would not overturn the sale contract.
Forestry Corp controls cutting rights to 188,000 hectares of pine and fir plantation forest in the central North Island as well as some nursery and milling operations.

The only citizens inititated referendum so far -- a push by the firefighters' union to maintain firefighter numbers -- got more than 400,000 signatures, but firefighters central branch secretary John Devereux estimated a third were classed invalid because of technicalities including the requirement for the signature to be dated and for an elector's address to be accurate.
Subsequent law changes have eased the rules on valid signatures and the Alliance should have far fewer signatures ruled out, spokesman John Pagani said.
His assessment was confirmed by Clerk of the House David McGee who does the initial sampling of petitions to establish they have the necessary number of names.
Pagani said the Alliance had vetted its petition and believed very few would be ruled out.
But firefighters union secretary Derek Best told Reuters that even under the less stringent requirements he estimated at least an eighth would be ruled invalid.
"They (the Alliance) absolutely will need at least 12 percent more than 240,000 and that is cutting it fine. We found that at least one in eight were not on the electoral roll," Best said.
That would suggest the Alliance would need at least 265,000 signatures to be sure it could force a referendum.
The Alliance wants to get the required signatures before the election, but has another nine months before the deadline for the referendum passes.

Pagani said Wednesday would be "a day of action" on the petition with the Alliance's electorate organisations taking a day off from the rest of the camapign to push it. The Alliance would release an updated figure on Friday.
On the same day the government will receive the cheque for Forestry Corp and plans to announce make political mileage from using the proceeds to wipe the government's net foreign debt.
